title: Properties of $\mathcal{O}_X(D)$
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme and $D\subset S$ an
effective Cartier divisor.

1. $\mathcal{O}_S(D)$ is an
invertible $\mathcal{O}_S$-module.
1. If $g:Y\to S$ is a flat morphism and $D_Y=D\times_SY$, then
$\mathcal{I}_{D_Y}=g^*\mathcal{I}_D$ and $\mathcal{O}_Y(D_Y)\cong g^*\mathcal{O}_S(D)$.

proof.text: (1) Let $\mathcal I_D\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ be the ideal sheaf of $D$. Since $D$ is an effective Cartier divisor, $\mathcal I_D$ is quasi-coherent and locally generated by one nonzerodivisor, i.e. an effective Cartier ideal. By [lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-invertible] its dual $\mathcal I_D^\vee=\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O_S}(\mathcal I_D,\mathcal O_S)$, which is $\mathcal O_S(D)$ by [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle], is an invertible $\mathcal O_S$-module. This is clause 1.

(2a) Now let $g:Y\to S$ be flat, $D_Y=D\times_SY$ with projection $q:D_Y\to Y$, and $\mathcal I_{D_Y}=\ker(\mathcal O_Y\to q_*\mathcal O_{D_Y})$. By [lem-pc-flat-pullback-effective-cartier-ideal] (applied to the effective Cartier ideal $\mathcal I_D$ of step (1)), $\mathcal I_{D_Y}$ is an effective Cartier ideal, so $D_Y$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $Y$ and $\mathcal O_Y(D_Y)=\mathcal I_{D_Y}^\vee$ is defined by [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle].

(2b) The identification $\mathcal I_{D_Y}=g^*\mathcal I_D$. Let $\iota:\mathcal I_D\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_S$ be the inclusion and $\epsilon_g:g^*\mathcal O_S\to\mathcal O_Y$ the morphism adjoint to $g^\sharp$, an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf]. By [lem-pc-closed-subscheme-base-change-ideal-image] (with $Z=D$, $i$ the closed immersion $D\to S$), $\mathcal I_{D_Y}$ is the image of $\phi=\epsilon_g\circ g^*(\iota):g^*\mathcal I_D\to\mathcal O_Y$. Since $g$ is flat, $g^*$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-pullback-exact-pushforward-injective]; applied to the exact sequence $0\to\mathcal I_D\xrightarrow{\iota}\mathcal O_S$ it shows that $g^*(\iota)$ is injective, hence so is $\phi$ ($\epsilon_g$ being an isomorphism). So $\phi$ is an isomorphism of $g^*\mathcal I_D$ onto its image $\mathcal I_{D_Y}$: under the canonical map $g^*\mathcal I_D\to\mathcal O_Y$, $\mathcal I_{D_Y}=g^*\mathcal I_D$. (Flatness is needed here: right exactness of $g^*$ only gives that $\mathcal I_{D_Y}$ is the image; for $D=V(x)\subset\mathbf A^1_k$ and $g$ the inclusion of the origin, $g^*\mathcal I_D\cong k\neq0=\mathcal I_{D_Y}$.)

(2c) By [lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-flat-pullback] (applied to $\mathcal I=\mathcal I_D$ and the flat $g$) there is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules $\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O_Y}(\mathcal I_{D_Y},\mathcal O_Y)\cong g^*\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O_S}(\mathcal I_D,\mathcal O_S)$, i.e. by step (2a) and [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] $\mathcal O_Y(D_Y)\cong g^*\mathcal O_S(D)$. With step (2b) this is clause 2.
